data.long_meaning: Opal is a precious stone, often valued for its unique and beautiful colors. It is not directly derived from any biblical or Christian tradition, but its name may come from the Sanskrit upala, meaning 'precious stone'. The name Opal carries the meaning “Precious stone” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Opal usually hope their child will grow to embody precious stone and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of transformation and inner beauty

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Opal total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_greek.name: Όπαλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Όπαλ είναι ο ονομάζεται ο λίθος που αναφέρεται στην Καινή Διαθήκη, με ποικίλους χρωματισμούς, συμβολίζει την ελπίδα και τον оптимισμό, η χρήση του στην πρώιμη χριστιανική εκκλησία ως σύμβολο της πίστης και της προσευχής

in_latin.name: Opalus
in_latin.long_meaning: Opalus est lapis qui in Novo Testamento commemoratur, variis coloribus, significat spem et optimismo, usus eius in ecclesia christiana primitiva ut symbolum fidei et orationis

in_english.name: Opal

data.cultural_impact: Opal has been associated with various beliefs and superstitions throughout history. In ancient Rome, it was believed to bring good fortune. Among the ancient Greeks, it was linked to hope and optimism. In Australia, indigenous people believed opal was created as a sign of the Creator's presence and power. Today, the gemstone opal is prized for its ability to reflect a full spectrum of light and for its unique patterns, which have inspired artists, writers, and poets.
data.spiritual_significance: In a Christian context, the name Opal could be seen as a reminder of the beauty and all-encompassing nature of God. The opal's unique patterns and colors may represent the diverse tapestry of God's creation. Additionally, the association of opal with hope, optimism, and good fortune could symbolize the hope and faith that believers hold in God and the blessings He provides. Ultimately, the name Opal could serve as a source of inspiration and a reminder of the wonder and majesty of God's creation.
